videos.speaker: Matthew Zivkovic (Lead Smart)
videos.title: How To Generate Calls for the Top Growing Pay Per Call Verticals
insights: Google and Microsoft search advertising, Facebook/Instagram social advertising, SEO and legitimate Google business listings are discussed as acquisition channels.
Essential home services are a major example vertical; this does not prove current roofing buyer-approved traffic or Empire performance.

videos.speaker: Adam Young (Ringba)
videos.title: Ringba and Pay Per Call – John Casto interview
insights: Keep independent call-source tracking and buyer-level outcome reports; publisher-provided numbers alone constrain optimisation.
Test differentiated relevant acquisition sources and do not copy competitor advertising or make unverified claims.
Use appropriate access-authorised call QA for mismatched creative, negative keyword proposals and buyer experience; not surveillance, unauthorised recordings or unsolicited retargeting.

videos.speaker: Ringba training team
videos.title: Ringba Product Training: Partner Management
insights: Publisher and buyer partner registration and self-service offer review can reduce manual onboarding.
Partner access/reporting permissions should distinguish publisher views, buyer views and founder-admin views.

videos.speaker: Ringba training team
videos.title: Ringba Product Training: Account Manager
insights: Different partner/team roles can access assigned call reporting with read-only or admin restrictions.
Read-only operator accountability beats exposing commercial call transcripts to every research agent.

videos.speaker: Ringba; Carlos Corona Jr; Dave Maman; Todd Schewber; Ankur Bhardwaj
videos.title: The Pay Per Call Journey: Miami Pay Per Call Mastermind
insights: Video description identifies operator interviews and roles; do not attribute undisclosed tactics, traffic or earnings from the video without a transcript.

videos.speaker: RingbaX
videos.title: How to View Call Logs and Block Channels
insights: Buyer-side training explicitly covers call logs and channel blocking; buyer decisions about eligible source quality should be documented separately.

videos.speaker: RingbaX
videos.title: How to Set Up a Seller Ring Tree and Ring Tree Target
insights: The seller-side video resource describes a ring-tree setup; actual routing rules must remain owned and unmodified pending current buyer authority.

findings: Buyer no-answer/busy disposition and fallback tracking can preserve consenting eligible call experiences; no automatic duplicate resale permission.
Source creative can generate cheap calls that do not fit the buyer, so source/qualification quality matters more than cheap CPC.
Ringba reported an early $45,000 revenue period in 2020, not an independently validated example of present profit or Empire performance.
Search, social and display sources were tested alongside existing media to reach a new market; campaign has industry-specific call qualification.
6,800 calls in 90 days and 50% conversion are the company's reported Medicare campaign results, not transferable roofing benchmarks.
A call-broker claims to connect qualified buyers and permitted publisher traffic without buying ads directly; terms/source rights and finance proof still necessary.

prioritized_actions.testable_evidence: First-party source-labeled page sessions, consented ZIP responses and mapped call handoffs; keep site publishing unchanged
Permitted aggregated reasons for no-answer/busy/wrong service/short duration/invalid ZIP and independent buyer acceptance; do not open protected recordings
Accepted source contract, call qualification, operating hours, buyers and publisher rights before partner onboarding or route changes
Buyer-authorised aggregate call-quality dispositions linked to queries and creative; proposals only, no live SEO or media edits
Keep reviewed video claims with dates, transcript/description distinction, current policy verification and not-an-ROI-guarantee status

disclosure: Some public pages contain excerpts or titles, not the full YouTube transcript. Other figures are first-party vendor/client marketing case claims, not audited results.

studies.label: Commercial buyer contract before launch
studies.observation: Networks describe buyer hours, caps, concurrent agents, payout, minimum connected duration, geographies and permitted marketing sources as offer conditions.
studies.implication: Require buyer-signed source terms, genuine receiving capacity and operating hours for each market before promoting any consumer call.
studies.prohibited_inference: Published buyer capacity means Empire buyer capacity

studies.label: Counterparty and broker depth transparency
studies.observation: Gene Morris recommends questioning claimed per-click payouts, learning how many intermediaries are between publisher and end buyer, and requesting qualified-call dispositions from affiliate managers.
studies.implication: Track counterparty chain, dispute path, written payable terms, reversal deadlines and who confirms original buyer acceptance.

studies.label: Owned publisher properties and alternative traffic
studies.observation: Anthony Sarandrea case describes vertical-specific owned media, multi-channel acquisition, unique marketing angles and integrated tracking instead of reliance on call-only search advertising.
studies.implication: Research existing genuine relevant organic and publisher audiences; preserve competitor SEO owner scope and do not mass-generate doorstep ZIP pages.
studies.prohibited_inference: Historical company call volumes or claimed 500% growth predict Empire results

studies.label: Creative/intent and qualification match
studies.observation: WeCall describes inexpensive calls that did not meet buyer needs and improved feedback by inspecting call reasons and quality.
studies.implication: CRO and paid/organic traffic learning should only use consented aggregate accepted versus rejected outcomes, matched to original campaign.
studies.prohibited_inference: Low CPC implies low payable call acquisition cost

studies.label: Buyer non-answer, busy and agent handling
studies.observation: Ringba QA documentation includes agents selectively ending calls, callbacks, bad call scripts, duration issues and two-sided publisher/buyer quality audits.
studies.implication: Record permitted reason-coded delivery/rejection counts; differentiate publisher defects from buyer non-answer, unavailable agent and commercial dispute; never replay calls to alternate buyers without authority.
studies.prohibited_inference: Every unaccepted call is a poor homeowner lead

studies.label: External answer-rate benchmark, not a roofing target
studies.observation: Invoca reports that 52% of inbound callers reach a person in its home services customers; 38% of answered calls are leads and 45% of those leads convert during the call. Study covers nine sub-industries (not a roofing-only benchmark).
studies.implication: Compare distinct answer, qualified lead and booked conversion outcomes without treating them as pay-per-call accepted or independently settled rates.
studies.prohibited_inference: Vendor samples equal Empire observed rates or roofing billable rates

studies.label: Google call-only ad deprecation
studies.observation: Google removed ability to create new call-only ads in February 2026, and plans for existing call ads to stop serving February 2027; responsive search ads with call assets are the supported transition.
studies.implication: Paid traffic research must not recommend creating old call-only ads; preserve paid spend at zero pending source permissions, buyer capacity and actual settlement economics.
studies.prohibited_inference: Historical call-only YouTube tutorial is a current account setup guide

studies.label: Consent-aware keyword and call source evidence
studies.observation: Invoca describes 15 June 2026 change making Google Consent Mode ad_storage decisive for Ads attribution; revoked consent can make conversions unattributed in Ads reports.
studies.implication: Preserve privacy-aware first-party lawful source and call lineage; do not backfill unknown sources with guesses or identify denied-consent visitors.
studies.prohibited_inference: Unattributed calls all came from a certain channel

studies.label: Publisher versus advertiser QA ownership
studies.observation: Ringba's network guide distinguishes publisher-source compliance from advertiser call-handling and finance reconciliation duties.
studies.implication: Use separate read-only QA reason codes and ownership while preserving original buyer acceptance authority; do not make downstream fraud allegations without evidence.

studies.label: Consent and unwanted calling restrictions
studies.observation: FTC distinguishes consumer-initiated enquiries from unsolicited outbound telemarketing and explains seller-specific prerecorded-call consent requirements and do-not-call obligations.
studies.implication: Do not equate an inbound homeowner request with permission for unsolicited calls; require jurisdiction-specific original-owner compliance review.
studies.prohibited_inference: A lead-generation form permits unlimited callback or resale

remaining_gaps: Original buyer source acceptance, payout and duration
Real paid/organic homeowner sessions by source
Actual Ringba buyer-leg answer and reason-code proportions
Current permitted advertising account setup and conversion tracking
